comparison: Both OpenEval and peer reviewers strongly support the experimental design and methodological details (C1-C4, C39-C62). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation while peer reviewers describe it as 'cleverly designed.' Both evaluations are fully aligned with SUPPORTED status.

Perfect agreement on behavioral findings (C6-C11). Both evaluations support the statistical results showing adaptation to volatility and unexpected responses to noise. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor while peer reviewers accept findings without challenge.

Complete alignment on modeling approach (C12-C18). Both evaluations praise the degraded BOM and systematic model comparison. Peer reviewers specifically highlight the 'creative approach' of lesioning the optimal model, matching OpenEval's positive assessment.

Full concordance on core finding about trial relabeling and misattribution (C19-C20, C28, C80). Both evaluations support this as the central result demonstrating imprecise noise estimation. Peer reviewers emphasize 'approximate rationality with simplified internal models.'

Strong agreement on pupillometry findings (C21-C23, C91). Both evaluations accept these as convergent physiological evidence. OpenEval emphasizes hierarchical regression validation while peer reviewers note 'convergent behavioural and pupillometric data' as strength. Peer result also includes C92 not in OpenEval R5.

Both support model selection procedures (C63-C65, C77-C78). OpenEval focuses on these specific claims while peer reviewers group broader methodological details (C67-C76) together. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with no substantive concerns.

OpenEval evaluates BOM implementation details (C67-C69) separately as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers include these claims within broader methodological acceptance (R6) without specific commentary on these implementation choices.

OpenEval separately evaluates alternative computational approach (C70-C72) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers subsume this within general methodological acceptance, noting 'model space could be more extensive' but accepting choices made.

OpenEval evaluates pupillometry preprocessing (C73-C76) as separate SUPPORTED result. Peer reviewers include these within broader methodological acceptance without specific focus on preprocessing procedures.

Perfect agreement on normative theoretical foundations (C25-C27, C29, C44). Both evaluations support these well-established principles from learning theory. OpenEval provides detailed justification while peer reviewers implicitly accept as established knowledge.

Both support characterization of prior literature (C24, C30-C31). OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer reviewers group with broader literature review (C32-C38, C83-C90, C97). Both are SUPPORTED.

Both support theoretical background claims (C32-C38). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of citations and logical flow while peer reviewers accept literature review without challenge as part of broader context.

OpenEval separately evaluates key design feature (C43, C57) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers include these within overall experimental design praise but don't specifically highlight this distinction from prior work.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C79, C81-C82, C85). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval traces support through behavioral, modeling, and pupillometry evidence. Peer reviewers emphasize 'approximate rationality' framework. Peer result also includes C96.

OpenEval rates claims about generalization (C83-C84, C86-C87) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about broader decision-making. Peer reviewers are SUPPORTED, accepting contextualization without expressing concern about generalization scope. This represents a divergence in evaluation.
Both support theoretical context claims (C88-C90). OpenEval evaluates these separately as SUPPORTED while peer reviewers include within broader literature acceptance without specific commentary.

OpenEval evaluates inferences from pupillometry (C92, C100) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate caution about neural implementation. Peer reviewers include C92 with pupillometry findings (R5) and C100 with limitations (R10), both SUPPORTED.

Both support acknowledgment of modeling limitations (C93-C96). OpenEval emphasizes distinction between algorithmic and implementation levels. Peer reviewers accept these limitations without challenge, grouping with C100.

Both support contextualization with neuroimaging literature (C97-C99). OpenEval evaluates separately as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate speculative framing. Peer reviewers include C97 within broader literature acceptance.

OpenEval evaluates clarification about measurement vs. mechanistic models (C101) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this distinction was not specifically addressed by reviewers.
